findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify S6's behavior when the ordered STATUS-hop trail is unavailable because the ticket has been compacted (STATUS events folded into a SNAPSHOT), since compiled_state does not preserve the ordered hop sequence.
evidence: Plan: S6 'derives the intended local hop sequence from the ticket's core STATUS event log ... re-attempts each intermediate hop ... in recorded order'
src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/inbound_translate.py:175 'a COMPACTED ticket — its STATUS events are folded into a SNAPSHOT and the standalone files are gone'
reducer/_replay.py + _cache.py confirm SNAPSHOT folding strips raw STATUS events; compiled_state carries the final status, not the ordered hop sequence
The felt-need concept 'the reconciler stores no hop history of its own' means the sole hop source is the core log — which is lossy under compaction
findings.finding: S6's replay mechanism derives the ordered hop sequence from the per-ticket STATUS event log, but a COMPACTED ticket has its STATUS events folded into a SNAPSHOT (standalone *-STATUS.json files removed) and the reducer's compiled_state preserves only the final status, not the ordered hop sequence — so the ordered trail the plan's replay depends on is unrecoverable for compacted tickets, and the plan does not specify what replay does in that case.
findings.location: Approach § (S6 transition replay); AC line 'A non-allowed transition is attempted by replay of rebar's recorded hops'; Child S6
scenarios: A long-lived ticket that has been compacted (SNAPSHOT written, standalone STATUS files removed) needs a non-allowed direct transition replayed
An old ticket bootstrapped from a SNAPSHOT with no post-snapshot STATUS events
findings.suggested_fix: State that a ticket whose ordered hop trail is unavailable (compacted / no standalone STATUS events) skips replay and drifts-with-warning — the same terminal answer as a rejected hop — and note the hop source is the raw append-only STATUS events, which compaction removes, so replay is best-effort by construction.

52b0 (S10) closing line: 'All four tiers run in-process, no live Jira, no specific CI provider — satisfying project.portability' — a portability-bearing child outside the S1–S8 range the docs claim references

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a short external prior-art note comparing the transition-replay algorithm and the rebar-type: collapse-label technique against how established cross-tracker sync tools (e.g. Exalate, k15t Backbone Issue Sync, getint) handle unreachable target statuses and lossy-value preservation, and justify rebar's chosen approach against them.
evidence: Approach: 'S6 adds new dispatcher logic that derives the intended local hop sequence from the ticket's core STATUS event log ... re-attempts each intermediate hop ... aborting to drift on the first hop the target rejects' — presented as new code with only internal-primitive grounding.

Approach: 'collapse (non-injective, e.g. epic→Initiative) made round-trip-safe by a rebar-type: label symmetric with today's rebar-status: labels' — a lossy-mapping-preservation technique with no external comparison.

Retrieved prior art solving the same problem space: Exalate 'Sync Status in Jira Cloud' (docs.exalate.com), k15t Backbone Issue Sync 'Bidirectional synchronization', getint 'Jira Azure DevOps Workflow & Status Mapping' (defined default statuses + controlled sync rules), Elements Copy & Sync 'workflow mappings to synchronize statuses'.

Retrieved Atlassian docs confirm the load-bearing constraint the replay algorithm targets: 'For a work item to move between two statuses, a transition must exist. Transitions are also one-way.' (support.atlassian.com create-workflow-transitions) — established sync tools already contend with reaching an unreachable status.
ABSENCE: plan enumerates internal prior art (ADR 0083/0055, config.md tooling survey) but names zero external tool or technique for the cross-tracker mapping/transition-reachability problem.
findings.finding: The plan cites no EXTERNAL prior art for a well-trodden problem domain — config-driven vocabulary mapping and unreachable-transition handling between issue trackers — and presents its two genuinely novel algorithmic pieces (transition replay from the status event log; the round-trip-safe rebar-type: collapse label) as invented-here without comparing them to how established cross-tracker sync tools solve the identical problems.
findings.location: Plan 'Approach' section (transition replay + collapse/rebar-type: label) and 'Acceptance Criteria' (transition-replay and type-collapse ACs)
scenarios: Design review asks whether transition-replay's 'walk the recorded hop sequence, abort on first rejection' is the state of the art or whether existing tools use a graph search over available transitions to a target status.
Reviewer asks whether the rebar-type: collapse-label round-trip technique matches or diverges from how Exalate/Backbone preserve lossy-mapped values on the sync partner.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure a881's priority-drift tests reset the shared _DRIFT_WARNED set (autouse reset_drift_warnings fixture) in whatever test file they live in, mirroring ab9f's status-file remedy.
evidence: a881: 'New shared helper resolve_outbound_priority(value, priority_map) -> str|None beside resolve_outbound_status (outbound_mapper.py:47) ... on miss → warn once (reset_drift_warnings sink, :31)'
a881 AC: 'test_priority_drifts — a priority absent from the effective map DRIFTS ... a warning is recorded'

ab9f: 'Add a module-scoped autouse pytest fixture to tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py that calls outbound_mapper.reset_drift_warnings() before each test' — scoped to a single module only
ab9f: 'the reconciler's outbound status/priority mapper keeps a process-global dedupe set _DRIFT_WARNED' — explicitly notes the set is shared by both status AND priority
findings.finding: The priority-drift path (a881's resolve_outbound_priority) writes the same process-global _DRIFT_WARNED dedupe set that ab9f identified as an order-dependency hazard, but ab9f's autouse reset fixture is scoped only to tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py — a881's new priority-drift tests (test_priority_drifts) live in a separate file and re-use the shared global with no corresponding reset, so they inherit the same latent test-order pollution ab9f exists to eliminate.
scenarios: Under pytest reordering, an earlier test records the priority value in _DRIFT_WARNED, so test_priority_drifts' 'a warning is recorded' assertion silently fails because the dedupe suppresses the second warning.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an autouse reset_drift_warnings() fixture to a881's priority test module (or move both drift suites under a shared conftest fixture) so every test writing _DRIFT_WARNED starts clean, matching ab9f's remedy for the status file.
